plugins.name: app-6a48e26850fc8191bbf8a086a61601cb
plugins.description: PhysioKeys helps clinicians, students, educators, and researchers search physiotherapy and rehabilitation evidence from ChatGPT. Users can search curated PhysioKeys records or PubMed, fetch article details, review abstracts and rights-verified cached full text when available, generate citations, view saved-article metadata, save PMIDs to their private library, and check account allowances. The plugin is intended only for de-identified research and citation workflows and may refuse requests containing patient-identifiable information. It does not provide emergency diagnosis or personalized medical advice.
plugins.author: Physiokeys

plugins.name: app-6a7b5a0c6f5c8191978777f40f445540
plugins.description: Placer.ai Pi answers business questions that turn on measured real-world behavior. Ask a full analytical question in plain language and Pi runs a complete Placer.ai analysis - foot traffic trends, visitor demographics and journeys, trade areas, cross-shopping, and sales and spend - then returns a written answer with data-honesty caveats, any web sources it used, and a deep link that opens the same analysis, with its interactive map, in Pi. A full analysis normally takes several minutes: ask_pi starts it and returns a handle, and get_pi_result collects the answer, reporting progress while the work runs. Typical workflows include store and portfolio performance, trade-area and site analysis, competitive benchmarking, tenant mix and co-tenancy review, market feasibility, and category or market-share tracking. Follow-up questions can reuse a previous analysis so the numbers stay consistent across a conversation. Access requires a Placer.ai account with Pi and the MCP access entitlement; Pi returns only the data the signed-in Placer user is entitled to see.
plugins.author: Placer.ai

plugins.name: app-6a37593da1d481918460edebfdc1a756
plugins.description: Piano 1024 is a playable synth piano inside ChatGPT. Learn songs phrase by phrase with fingering and hands-separate practice; build chord progressions and melodies you refine across the conversation; hear and name any chord; keep a metronome in any meter; and train your ear with graded interval, chord, and scale drills. Every note is synthesized live on the in-chat keyboard — tap to play, no samples or setup. Part of the 1024 family of music tools.
plugins.author: Kyung-Hoon Kim

plugins.name: app-6aa2be7123248191bd3ef3b14ed4f730
plugins.description: Piazza in Festa answers questions about what is happening in Italian towns: village feasts, patron saint festivals, food and wine fairs, street markets, concerts and exhibitions. The catalogue is rebuilt every day from the notices that town halls are legally required to publish on their official register, so it also covers very small towns that no other calendar lists. Users can search by town, region, category, free text or date range, open a single event for practical details such as dates, venue and organiser, and ask which towns are covered in a region. Every result carries a link to the event page and to the official document it was derived from, so answers can be verified.
plugins.author: Lorenzo Iovino

plugins.name: app-69610ef30e448191aed57cd6074249a3
plugins.description:
pickyourmatch finds travellers the exact bookable accommodation — not a room category. Every unit is individually described down to the view, the floor, the beds and the per-unit child and dog allowance, with data refreshed nightly from each property's GauVendi system.

Ask for "an apartment in Schladming for 2 adults, 2 kids and a dog, 16–19 August" and the app returns units that are actually available for those dates, with the real nightly rate and a direct booking link that opens the property's own booking calendar with the exact unit and dates preselected — no portals, no middleman, no fees on top.

Also included: themed promotions and packages (dog holidays, romance, wellness, culinary) with included extras, searchable by city or theme. The app is read-only, needs no account and processes no personal data.
plugins.author: GauVendi GmbH

plugins.name: app-6ab55e5b36708191aaba731d3e039444
plugins.description: Pickaxe helps users inspect and manage resources within their authorized Pickaxe workspaces, including AI agents, knowledge, deployments, portals, users, and memory, and run agents directly from ChatGPT.
plugins.author: Pickaxe

plugins.name: app-6a9f7b2b538081918d33c60ccd00792e
plugins.description: PickFu runs polls and surveys with real, targeted consumer panels so you can test decisions before you commit. Ask a question — compare two product images, headlines, logos, app icons, or names — and get ranked results with written explanations from real people in the demographic you choose, usually within minutes. Build a poll, launch it to a targeted audience, and read the results (the winner, the vote breakdown, and respondents' comments) without leaving the chat. Built for marketers, founders, designers, and product teams who want evidence instead of guesses.
plugins.author: PickFu

plugins.name: app-6a98926fdab081919b016b0bc29fd5f2
plugins.description:
pickthehotel is an answer engine for hotels. Instead of a wall of results, ask for the one hotel that fits your intent in a city and get a single confident pick, a few alternatives, and a booking link.

Choose an intent:
• iconic - the standout in town
• value - great, and fairly priced for what you get
• budget - cheap, clean, and genuinely central
• family - one room that actually sleeps two adults and the children

Every hotel is judged the same way - value (punching above its price), location (closeness to what you actually came for), and reviews (weighted by confidence, not just averaged) - with no paid placement. You can anchor "central" to a landmark ("near the Louvre") or to your live location, and you can ask for a curated list of long-established hotels around the world.

Live in Zürich, Paris, London, New York, Tokyo, Bangkok, Dubai, Singapore, Istanbul, and Hong Kong, with more rolling out. Prices are indicative and confirmed at the booking site; booking links are affiliate and disclosed.
plugins.author: SYLVAIN CHRISTOPHER ALEXANDER GORDON-HORWOOD

plugins.author: PicPay

plugins.author: Picsart

plugins.name: app-6aa6d22a487c819195f5f691e628aa01
plugins.description: Create private illustrated storybooks from your ideas, follow generation progress, and read stories saved in your PictureBooks account. Built for parents, caregivers, educators, and other adult authors. Connect your existing account to check available credits and create books using those credits. The plugin does not purchase credits, charge a card, or publish your books. You can disconnect access in PictureBooks at any time.
plugins.author: WILSON GAN

plugins.description: Pierview helps users track and improve their brand's visibility across AI search platforms such as ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Deepseek, and Grok. Through this app, users can pull mention rate, ranking, and share-of-voice metrics, see which domains and pages are citing their brand, compare visibility and sentiment against competitors, review traffic sent by AI assistants, check technical AI-SEO audit results, read and update their brand kit guidelines, and generate narrated performance reports for any date range.
plugins.author: Pierview AI Inc.

plugins.name: app-6a5d193da3688191ac49e79b08d3d876
plugins.description: PiggyTask helps parents organize kids’ chores with coins and rewards. Connect once with OAuth, then ask ChatGPT to list children, create mandatory or bonus tasks, assign pool tasks, or mark chores done. Access stays scoped to the family you approve and can be revoked anytime in PiggyTask settings. PiggyTask is independent and not affiliated with OpenAI.
plugins.author: Keith

plugins.name: app-6aaeb317713c8191a7432b0b54586a89
plugins.description:
Pile Capacity estimates the axial bearing and uplift capacity of cast-in-situ bored piles and CFA piles from a soil profile and a pile schedule, and solves the inverse problem: the length each pile needs to carry a stated compression and tension load.

Describe the ground and the piles in plain language, such as layer thicknesses and types, undrained shear strength or friction angle, rock UCS, groundwater level, pile diameters, target loads and factors of safety. The connector resolves that into a complete analysis input and shows you the resolved input, every assumption it had to make for a value you did not give, and the provenance of each field (your value, an engineering convention, or a default), so you confirm or correct the design before anything is calculated.

Confirmed designs return one summary per pile: required length, toe level, allowable and ultimate compression and uplift capacity, and the factors used. You can then render the full calculation report as a PDF with charts, formulas and per-layer tables, or as an Excel workbook with live formulas, and save the design into a project in your Pile Capacity account, where it opens in the web app like any other design.

SI and US customary units are both supported. The connector picks the system from the units you write and warns you when your words and your numbers disagree.

Requires a hetGE account with an active Pile Capacity licence. Sign-in is OAuth against id.hetge.com; the connector never sees your password and reads only the design inputs your assistant sends, plus at most one sentence of your wording when it contains unit words, used only to check the units.
plugins.author: hetGE LLC

plugins.name: app-6aafd241175c819186db1fe910bdc783
plugins.description: Pillr gives free, no-login access to French real estate public data: the price per square meter for any municipality, a market summary (rent, yield, price trends, zoning), and the permit or declaration requirements for a renovation project. Every figure is sourced from official public data (DVF, DHUP, INSEE) and French urbanism law, with no listings, no addresses, and no proprietary scoring shown.

PlatoForms is an online form builder for web forms, fillable PDF forms and PDF documents. This plugin connects your PlatoForms account so you can work with your own forms and their submissions in conversation, instead of opening the dashboard.

What you can do

• Find forms. List published, draft or archived forms with their folder, publish state and submission count, or search by name.

• Understand a form. Read a form's full field schema — every field's id, type, label, whether it is required, its options and its validation rules — so you can reason about the data before you touch it.

• Review submissions. List a form's submissions newest-first, filter them by date range or keyword, find one by an exact field value (for example the submission where the email field is a particular address), and read every answer of a single submission with its field labels.

• Export. Mint a time-limited download URL for a submission's PDF, CSV, signing certificate, zipped attachments or a single attachment. Files are never streamed through the conversation — you get a link that expires.

• Share a prefilled link. Create one or more tracked invitation links to a form with fields already filled in, optionally single-use, optionally with an expiry. The plugin returns the URLs for you to send; it never sends email itself.

• Submit an entry. Post an entry to a published form after reading its schema, with validation errors returned verbatim so mistakes can be corrected and resubmitted.

• Start something new. Describe a form or a PDF document in plain English and get a builder link back. The design happens in the PlatoForms builder when you open the link, with its own AI asking you the clarifying questions.

How it connects

Sign in with your PlatoForms account over OAuth — your password is never shared with the assistant, access is scoped to read or read-and-write, and you can revoke it at any time from your PlatoForms account. The plugin can only see what your own account can see.

plugins.description:

Plan and schedule
Draft a post, choose which of your connected accounts it goes to, attach an image or video, and place it on the calendar for a specific time. Save it as a draft, route it for approval, or approve one that is already waiting. Review what is queued and remove a scheduled post. Add an account
Generate a link that opens PostFast's account connection flow when you want to add a new social profile.

How it works
PostFast connects to each social network under its own app registrations and platform credentials, and stores your drafts, scheduled posts, media and comment history in your own PostFast workspace. This plugin is a first-party interface to that product, not a generic pass-through layer. Some tools do call a platform live, for example when publishing a post, and each of those is labelled as such.

You sign in with your existing PostFast account over OAuth. Viewing accounts, writing posts, and reading analytics are separate permissions that you grant individually, and you can disconnect at any time. The connector also exposes comment management tools used by other clients, which are not part of the workflows described here.

plugins.name: app-6a7ae2565a148191802be85a9bf06ab2
plugins.description:
Postify is a social media scheduling tool for teams: one calendar for the accounts you publish to, with drafts, scheduling, and delivery analytics in one place. The Postify plugin lets ChatGPT work that calendar with you: list posts and open a specific one, see which channels are connected, draft a new post, move a scheduled post to a different time, search your media library for an image you already uploaded, ask for a suggested posting time, publish a post immediately, or delete one. It can also pull performance figures for posts already delivered, and search Postify's own documentation when you need to know how something works.

Access runs through OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, and issued tokens are bound to the Postify MCP endpoint. You choose scopes on the consent screen, and a tool whose scope you did not grant is never registered for the session, so the assistant cannot see it. Connected apps are listed in Settings and can be revoked there, and every tool call is written to an audit log you can read in the app.

The two irreversible actions — publishing and deleting — are deliberately gated twice. First, an organization setting controls whether an AI assistant may perform them at all, and that setting can only be turned on by a person inside Postify; no AI credential carries the scope needed to enable it. Second, with the setting on, the first call returns a confirmation request with a short-lived token bound to the exact arguments, which must be echoed back on a second call before anything is published or deleted. Expect that first response — it is the safety step working, not an error.

plugins.description:
Web search returns abstracts, paywalls, and citations that cannot be checked. Redpine returns the relevant chunk of the document.

Redpine licenses full-text research directly from publishers and research institutions, and serves it to ChatGPT/Codex over MCP alongside a large open-access corpus. One query searches both.

Provenance by default. Every result carries its publisher, title, publication date, and a resolvable identifier such as a DOI. Licensed content and open-access content are labeled separately, so the two are never confused inside an answer.

You see the price first. Any search can be previewed for free. ChatGPT/Codex sees the title, source, and a snippet of every result, plus the exact cost to unlock them, then asks before spending anything. Unlock the three results that matter instead of the 30 that came back. The same results re-fetch free for seven days. Discovery, schema inspection, previews, and balance checks are always free.

Built for questions where being wrong is expensive. Clinical decisions, systematic review, research engineering, and any analysis that has to survive a source check.

An account can also hold data integrations beyond literature. ChatGPT/Codex reads what that account is entitled to at runtime rather than assuming a fixed tool list.

Compensation flows back to the rights holders. New accounts get free queries. Credits are bought on the Redpine dashboard, and the connector never handles payment details: it shows the price and asks before anything is charged.

Requires a Redpine account. Sign-in is OAuth on first use.
plugins.author: Redpine Technology AB

plugins.description: Reecopedia searches the primary texts of EU textile sustainability law and returns the matching passages with their source file and page, so answers can be checked against the document instead of trusted. The corpus covers ESPR (Regulation (EU) 2024/1781), the Digital Product Passport, CSRD, CBAM, EU ETS, CWA 18291 (CIRPASS-2) and the JRC preparatory studies for textiles. Typical workflows: ask a compliance question and get cited passages; browse a result list and open a full document page; walk the outline of a standard and jump to the section you need; locate an exact wording such as an article number inside one document. It never browses the open web and never writes the answer itself. When the retrieved passages match poorly it says so, and when the only match is a EUR-Lex national-transposition register card it warns that the date on that card is a notification date and not an entry into force. No account and no personal data are required.

plugins.description:
Revenue Analytics by DataLabs.store connects your HubSpot data to ChatGPT. It continuously replicates your portal (custom objects, deals, contacts, companies, line items, engagements, email events) into a real relational Microsoft SQL Server database whose schema matches your portal, then lets ChatGPT query it in plain English and return answers backed by the exact SQL that produced them.

Why it exists
HubSpot is built to run your CRM at scale, and its reporting tools are genuinely good at what they were designed for. The limit is structural: standard reports are built one object at a time, so questions that need several tables joined together before the math even starts do not fit. Per-deal margin (deals joined to their line items), multi-hop paths (deal to contact to company to source), correctly weighted stats (SUM(clicks)/SUM(delivered), not an average of averages), cohorts, and window functions all need a real database underneath. That is the job this fills.

What you can ask
- "Rank owners by weighted pipeline (each deal's amount times its real stage odds) and their historical win rate."
- "Unique click-through rate by acquisition source, weighted by delivered volume, for contacts who became customers."
- "Which deals are aging past 90 days, and where does our ARR actually concentrate?"
Then keep drilling: "now split by pipeline... now only Q2... now show the trend."

What makes it different
- Real joins across any objects, expressed as one query.
- Every answer is auditable: the exact SQL ships with the number, so you can verify and reproduce it.
- You bring the model: full frontier ChatGPT reasoning runs over your own data.
- Complementary to HubSpot's own AI. Breeze works inside the CRM; this understands the data behind it.

A note on sensitive data
This app's HubSpot integration requests only standard, non-sensitive OAuth read scopes for CRM analytics. It does not request HubSpot's sensitive scope grants (for example, crm.objects.contacts.sensitive.read).
plugins.author: DataLabs.store

Riveter turns web research into structured data. Give Claude a list of companies, people, or URLs and ask for new columns: product descriptions, revenue, deep analysis, company headcount, link traces, pricing, tech stack analysis, contact details, a classification, a summary, etc. Riveter runs an AI agent per row that searches, reads pages, and fills in each cell with a sourced answer.

What you can do

- Enrich rows you already have. Paste a list or point at a saved enrichment and get the new columns back. Up to 10,000 rows per run.
- Build a list from a description. "Every lawfirm in Indiana", "every YC W24 company in healthcare", "competitors of Stripe". Riveter generates the rows, and can enrich them in the same run.
- Scrape a page. Clean text or markdown from any URL, including JavaScript-rendered pages.
- Search the web. One-shot search results, or a research agent that answers a question with a structured, schema-shaped response.
- Extract records from a site. Define the fields you want and pull them from listings, directories, or catalogs as JSON.
- Monitor for changes. Run a saved enrichment daily, weekly, or monthly and get alerts or webhooks when values change.

How it works

Long runs are asynchronous. Claude starts the run, checks status, and fetches results when they are ready. Every run has an id you can come back to later, and results stay available in your Riveter account.

plugins.description:
Rosey is an independent verification layer for documents, decks, or other content that has been drafted, edited, or summarized by AI — financial reports, scientific writing, technical documentation, and any other content where factual precision matters.

Rosey checks Accuracy: every claim, number, and citation in a document is verified against its source materials, with findings delivered as traceable evidence rather than a bare confidence score. It also applies optional expert personas — a CFO reviewing for financial coherence, an adversarial analyst stress-testing claims, an operating partner checking operational plausibility — to surface weaknesses before an output reaches its intended audience.

Why it matters for agentic workflows: an agent that generates important outputs for users or agents downstream cannot reliably verify its own output. Verification benefits from a separate system checking claims against ground truth, the same way external audit is separate from the finance team it reviews. Rosey is built for end-users, agents, and agentic pipelines so that errors can be caught before they propagate – either to another agent or to someone who will make decisions based on the output. 

Findings are returned with in-line judgement on each factual claim, so work can move from draft → verified → finalized quickly.

Typical triggers: a document contains numerical claims, financial figures, or factual assertions; a document was generated or substantially edited by an AI model; a document is headed to a client, regulator, or decision-maker and needs a pre-send accuracy check; an agent is creating important output that will be consumed as inputs by another agent in a workflow and requires reliability.

Not for: scenarios where there is not an underlying source-of-truth that can be provided directly to Rosey.
plugins.author: InSummary

Sellergoo is a profit-and-operations analytics service for online sellers. You connect the shops, marketplaces, payment and accounting accounts you already sell through, and Sellergoo brings the orders, fees, refunds, cost of goods, advertising and overhead together to work out what you actually earned — per channel, per product, per order.

This plugin lets you ask about those numbers in plain language instead of exporting spreadsheets. Ask what last month really made after fees, which SKUs are thin on margin, what a marketplace actually deposited in your bank account, or which products run out of stock first.

READ-ONLY
This plugin can only look. It cannot place, cancel, refund, reprice or change anything — not in Sellergoo, and not in any shop or marketplace you have connected. Every tool it exposes is read-only, and the access you grant it carries no permission to write. It reads figures that already belong to you, in answer to questions you ask.

WHAT IT CAN ANSWER
• Profit — sales, units, refunds, fees, cost of goods, ad spend, overhead, gross and net profit, margin and ROI for a period, combined and per channel.
• Profit and loss — a month-by-month P&L for up to the last 12 months, all channels or one.
• Orders — any date range, paginated, with each order's sales and marketplace fees.
• Products — per-SKU sales, units, margin and profit for a period, ranked by sales.
• Payouts — the settlements marketplaces and payment providers actually paid out, with the amounts grouped by line type.
• Inventory — stock on hand, 30-day sell-through and days of cover per SKU, one sales channel at a time.
• Alerts — stock-outs, low stock, thin margins, lost Buy Box, price changes and negative reviews.
• Channels — which shops are connected and when each last synced.

WHAT YOU NEED
A Sellergoo account (sellergoo.com). You sign in once and approve the connection; nothing is copied or pasted by hand. The answers are only as complete as the accounts you have connected — a brand-n

Sendly is an email platform for product teams: a transactional sending API, campaigns, visual workflow automations, contacts with custom fields, lists, dynamic segments, topic preferences, suppressions, sending-domain setup and analytics. The Sendly plugin lets ChatGPT run that workspace from your own account: look up contacts and segments, explain how last week's emails performed, draft a campaign or a template, build a multi-step onboarding workflow from a plain-language brief, check why mail from a domain is not landing, validate addresses, manage suppressions and topics, and — only when you explicitly confirm — send.

Sending is treated as the dangerous action it is. Access runs through OAuth 2.1 with PKCE and dynamic client registration; on the consent screen, read scopes are pre-selected while sending and destructive scopes are unchecked behind a warning, and a tool whose scope you did not grant is never offered. Sending a campaign is two-step: the first call reports the audience size and asks, and only a second call carrying an explicit confirmation sends. Test sends can reach only your own verified address. Mail can only go out from domains you have verified, every project has daily and monthly sending caps tied to its trust tier, and destructive tools are annotated so clients can ask before running them.

The plugin sells nothing in-tool, generates no images, video or audio, and serves no ads. Address validation and list cleaning are metered features of your Sendly plan.

plugins.description:
SentinelX lets you manage your Linux, macOS, and Windows servers from ChatGPT — no SSH required. Install a small open-source agent on any Linux, macOS, or Windows host, and ChatGPT can run inspection commands, manage services (systemd, launchd, or Windows services), read/search/edit files, run scripts, upload files, and call out to integrations like Cloudflare DNS, Resend, and Telegram.

Every action is constrained by a per-host allowlist that you control. The agent only runs commands and services you've explicitly declared safe, rejects anything outside the policy at the agent boundary, and your OS's file permissions still apply on top. You can connect multiple hosts and label them however you want.

Typical uses: check uptime and disk space, restart services, tail logs, edit config files, run quick scripts, manage DNS records, send notifications. The agent is open source on GitHub (github.com/pensados/sentinelx-cloud-core). Authentication uses OAuth 2.0 with PKCE and Dynamic Client Registration, scoped per user.

You can ask why a move is good, why a move is bad, what to do next, or how to get better. This app is made for people who want to play, learn, and have fun at the same time.

The app is easy to use. Just begin a game and make your moves. You can use simple move names, standard chess notation, or ask questions in plain English. If you are not sure what to do, ask for help. The game keeps going while you chat, so learning feels natural instead of like reading a long lesson.

If you are brand new to chess, this app is a friendly place to start. It explains ideas in small, simple steps. It tells you what each piece can do and why some moves are stronger than others. You never have to pretend you understand. Just ask another question. You can learn one move at a time.

If you already know how to play, you can go deeper. Talk about openings, middle games, endgames, tactics, strategy, planning, and common mistakes. Ask why a position feels better for one side. Compare different moves. Explore new ideas. The conversation changes to fit your questions.

Play at your own speed. Think for a long time or move quickly. Stop to ask about a position. Go back and look at an earlier move. Try a different idea and see what could happen. Chess is not only about finding the best move. It is also about understanding why that move works.

The app can explain forks, pins, skewers, discovered attacks, double checks, sacrifices, passed pawns, king safety, piece activity, space, time, and many other chess ideas using clear language. Hard topics become easier because you can ask for another explanation whenever you need one.

plugins.description:
Socra Cortex helps people and teams stop repeating the same preferences, requirements, and decisions to ChatGPT and Codex. It keeps that knowledge and its reasons in a single source of truth that agents can retrieve before acting, across conversations and tools.

Modules record what should be and why, with a responsible owner and version history. Dependencies link the knowledge required to understand it. Flash loads the relevant Module and all its Dependencies, foundations first and each Module once.

Team members can own different subjects while their knowledge works together. For example, a product requirement Module created in ChatGPT can depend on architecture and security Modules maintained by their owners. Codex can Flash that requirement before implementing it and receive those decisions together.

As conversations and work reveal new knowledge, agents propose changes to existing Modules, so the knowledge always stays up to date. The suggested workflow asks them to show exact Before and After content and Dependencies for the owner's approval before saving. Updates become available on later Flashes, while version history preserves earlier knowledge and records changes.

Issues connect tasks to the Modules governing them, with assignees, work dependencies, comments, and evidence. Inboxes show unblocked work to its responsible person or agent; completed Issues preserve the outcome and history.

People and teams own the knowledge in their Socra Account, with Module permissions for people and groups. Review Modules, the knowledge map, and work at https://cortex.socra.com. Connect ChatGPT, Codex, or any other AI provider to that same Account with Cortex access.

Setup and agent instructions: https://workspace.socra.com/docs/cortex/installation.md

plugins.description:
StrategyTune is a backtesting platform for trading strategies, and this plugin gives ChatGPT hands-on access to it.

ChatGPT can write and save the pieces you build with — chart indicators, reusable market conditions (StrategyTune calls them signals and filters), and full trading strategies — then run them tick-by-tick against real historical market data in StrategyTune's sandboxed cloud. A simple strategy backtests a year of history in seconds, so you can iterate fast.

It is not limited to automated strategy backtesting. ChatGPT can run custom research code in the same sandbox: count how often a condition occurred, measure values at specific moments, gather your own statistics and write logs during the run. You say what you want to check, ChatGPT writes the code, runs it, reads the output back, and tells you what it found.

When a run finishes you get the full report — performance statistics and the individual trades behind them. ChatGPT can also work with a StrategyTune chart you already have open: read the bars and each indicator's computed values, add and configure indicators, mark those conditions on the timeline so you can see exactly when they held, and switch instrument or timeframe. Reading the computed values also lets it debug its own work: if an indicator it wrote looks wrong on your chart, it can check the actual numbers behind the line instead of guessing.

Everything runs on historical data. The plugin does not connect to a broker, place live orders, or give investment advice.
plugins.author: StrategyTune

plugins.description: Stratta answers civil and structural engineering questions from the norms your own organization has uploaded under its own license, and it answers them with a citation you can check: the exact section path and the page number. Each organization brings its own copies; Stratta hosts no shared corpus and redistributes no standard. The agent opens the table of contents, walks down to the clause that matters, reads it, follows the cross-references that change the answer, and looks at the figure when a load diagram carries the rule. Project dossiers keep the trail of what was retained, what it rests on, and what is still open: the questions of a dossier, their options, their evidence with every citation field, the decision and the remarks left along the way. For a site in Switzerland, the agent can also read the site sheet the app builds from public cantonal and federal registers, with its boreholes and their strata, and open one for an address on the plans that include it. The office's own owners and administrators can file a norm they hold a licence for from their own machine, through the ingestion tools. A new workspace starts with DEMO 001, a fictional document written by Stratta, so the workflow can be tried before any licensed norm is uploaded.

plugins.name: app-69528c304ff08191865579052e70b158
plugins.description:
trainedby.ai connects your wearables to ChatGPT, so your AI coach knows your real training load, sleep patterns, and recovery without you typing a word.

**The problem with AI fitness coaching today**

People are turning to ChatGPT to plan their marathon training, strength programs, or HYROX prep. It makes sense, because AI is available 24/7, extremely patient, and quite knowledgeable.

But somehow it doesn't quite work.

And that is because you have to tell it everything. Every. Single. Time.

Every conversation starts from zero. You have to describe in detail your current level, recent workouts, schedule, and goals. You paste in screenshots from Garmin. You try to remember what you did last week, how you slept, that your resting HR has been elevated, or that your HRV has been trending down for weeks.

The advice is based on what you told it, not what actually happened.

And what you tell it is incomplete, subjective, and often wrong.

What if your AI coach could see everything?

We connect your wearables (Garmin, Oura, Whoop, Apple Health, and 50+ other platforms) directly to your AI assistant.

When you open ChatGPT and ask about your training, it already knows:
- Workouts from the past weeks, months, and year
- Sleep quality and patterns
- Heart rate variability and resting heart rate trends
- Daily activity and recovery metrics
- Nutrition and menstrual cycle data (if you track it)

No more context dumps. No more subjective self-reporting.

**How it works**

We use smart compression to turn weeks of wearable data into something an AI can understand and analyze. Instead of dumping raw heart rate readings into a chat window, we surface the trends and patterns that matter—elevated resting HR, declining HRV, increasing training load, poor sleep consistency.

Personalized and Proactive Assistance: TwinMind provides tailored suggestions and ideas based on your captured memories, anticipating needs and offering relevant insights.

An information and calculation tool for visa applications by citizens of Türkiye (ordinary/burgundy passport).

It answers questions like "Do I need a visa for Japan?", "How much does a German visa cost?" and "How many Schengen days do I have left?" — always with its source.

What it covers:

· Visa status for 172 countries — 55 visa-free, 23 visa on arrival, 30 e-visa, 64 requiring a consulate application
· Per country: the fee, the published processing time, the application centre and the required documents
· Refusal rates for Schengen applications made from Türkiye, based on European Commission statistics (27 countries)
· Appealing a refusal: the competent authority, deadline, language and fee for seven Schengen countries, and the meaning of all 17 refusal grounds on the standard form
· Calculators: the Schengen 90/180 day allowance, multiple-entry (cascade) eligibility, and the total cost in Turkish lira at the central bank rate

How the data is collected:

Every amount and duration is verified against an official consulate, ministry or legislative source, quoted verbatim. A value that cannot be verified is not published — nothing is estimated; the field is left empty and said to be empty. Answers carry their source and last-updated date.

Only the consulate of the country concerned can grant a visa. We are not an agency: we do not file applications, book appointments, or guarantee approval.

plugins.description:
Ask about a US election — the 2026 midterms ahead, or any presidential election since 1788 — and get an answer with a date on it.

For 2026: the consensus competitiveness rating for any of the 100 Senate seats and 435 House districts, a consensus of Cook Political Report and Sabato's Crystal Ball, along with which races are genuinely in play and what forecasters have changed their minds about since the last update.

The part a chat assistant cannot do on its own is the arithmetic. Describe a scenario in plain language — "Republicans hold every toss-up but lose Maine" — and VoteMapper resolves it against the ratings in effect and returns a full chamber map you can argue with. Click any race to reassign it and the tally follows. The Senate has 65 seats that are not on the 2026 ballot and are already counted; getting that right is the difference between a real answer and a confident wrong one.

For history: every presidential election from 1788 to 2024, as a map rather than a paragraph. Compare two elections and see which states changed hands, trace one state's whole voting history and current streak, or reassign states to ask what a different outcome would have meant. Multi-way elections like 1860 and 1912 come back whole rather than flattened into two parties.

You can also check a sealed VoteMapper forecast. A prediction declared in the app is verified here by fingerprint and scored against published race calls once results land — over called races only, so an uncalled race is never counted as a miss.

VoteMapper is a simulator. It reports no live vote counts, returns or called races, and its historical data holds electoral votes, not popular-vote totals. Every answer carries the date its data was published, both parties are treated symmetrically throughout, and the connector takes no position on any race.

Read-only and stateless: no account, no sign-in, nothing written, nothing retained between requests.

Who What Wear brings the women's fashion publication's editorial voice into ChatGPT. It works like having a stylist who already knows your taste — once you've set up a short style profile, every fashion question gets a personalised, brand-aware answer instead of a generic one.

Setup takes about a minute. A guided four-step widget asks for your style words (Low-Key Luxury, Tailored, French, Sporty, Trend-Forward and others), the brands you actually shop across contemporary, luxury, denim and accessories, the style icons whose looks you'd happily borrow, and the price range you're comfortable with. The profile is saved per user, so it carries across conversations rather than starting over every time you open ChatGPT.

After onboarding, three things become useful.

Shopping for a specific item. Tell the app what you're looking for — "find me a black blazer under £250", "I need a coat for a winter wedding", "what jeans should I buy" — and it returns three to five picks weighted toward the brands you already buy from, plus a complete outfit built around the piece: what to wear on top, on the bottom, on your feet, and one or two accessories. The aim is to leave with a wearable answer, not a list of links.

Editorial inspiration. Ask what you should be wearing or looking at right now, and the app pulls fresh articles from Who What Wear UK's live editorial feed, then picks the two or three that match your taste using the brand and category tags on each article. The picks render as a horizontal carousel of cards in the publication's own visual language: editorial image, kicker, headline, byline credit, and a link straight back to the article on whowhatwear.com.

Refining your profile. Taste shifts. Reopen the onboarding to update any answer (and only the answers you want to change), or reset the profile entirely if you're starting fresh.

A few things worth knowing. The editorial feed is Who What Wear UK, so the content leans British in voice, currency and seasonality. Reco

WisdomAI is the enterprise data harness inside ChatGPT, for the complex analytical questions where the answer has to be deterministic, traceable, and consistent.

Connectors provide access. Catalogs and semantic layers provide definitions. The WisdomAI harness applies both at runtime by selecting the right context for each question, enforcing row- and column-level security for the person asking, optimizing execution for the underlying platform, verifying results, and repairing failed queries.

Business context strengthens continuously as WisdomAI learns from documents, query logs, catalogs, semantic layers, dbt, and BI metadata, proactively identifies where it lacked sufficient context, and routes proposed changes through expert review and versioning. Corrections become governed organizational knowledge rather than one-time fixes buried in individual conversations.

WisdomAI works across data platforms, sources, and deployment environments, including fully on-premises for regulated data that cannot leave your environment. The harness, the context, and query execution stay behind your firewall; only the answer crosses.

Every answer is grounded in governed definitions, enterprise data, and visible sources making it trustworthy enough to run your business on.

Use WisdomAI in ChatGPT to:
- Ask questions of governed business data: "How did Q3 net revenue track against plan in EMEA?"
- Follow up in the same line of analysis: "Break that down by segment and show the last 4 quarters"
- Investigate an open-ended question end to end: "We missed plan in EMEA last quarter. What drove it, which segments and accounts moved most, and what should we watch going into Q4?"
- Trace an answer to its definitions and sources: "Which definition of net revenue was used, and what data did it come from?"
- See what's available to you: "What data do I have access to, and which metrics are defined for finance?"

plugins.description:
For people in Japan who want to sell a used motorcycle, moped or scooter.

What this app does
- Model identification: from a loose description such as "the 150cc Honda PCX" or "a 50cc scooter I used to ride", it matches the vehicle against our dataset of 842 models. Models not in the dataset are directed to a phone consultation.
- Estimated buyback price by condition: an estimate in Japanese yen across five condition grades - like-new, running/very good, running/typical for its age, running with damage or faults, and non-running or accident-damaged.
- Request a free on-site appraisal: it submits the customer's name, phone number, area and model, then returns a reference number. The appointment is NOT fixed at that moment; our staff call back to agree the date. Up to three preferred times can be included (all optional).

Service area
Seven prefectures: Kanagawa, Tokyo, Saitama, Chiba, Ibaraki, Gunma and Yamanashi. The area widens as we add partner dealers. Travel, appraisal and cancellation are all free of charge.

Who carries out the appraisal
Every request is received by UsedBikeCenter ZAMA and we handle all first contact. Inside Kanagawa we visit and buy directly. In the other six prefectures we introduce a partner secondhand-goods dealer, and that partner carries out the on-site appraisal and the purchase; we act as the introducer and receive a referral fee. In those cases the request details - name, phone number, area, model, condition, preferred times and notes - are shared with that partner and used only to arrange and carry out the appraisal. This is stated in our privacy policy.

Before anything is sent
The tool first returns a preview of the request together with the sharing notice above. It transmits only after the customer has reviewed it and given explicit consent. Until then the tool returns the preview only.

No payments inside ChatGPT
This app only looks up price estimates and submits a request for a free appraisal. There is no payment, checkout, orde

plugins.description:
Chashmalink answers questions about Israeli household electricity from measured smart-meter data rather than estimates off a bill.

Behind it sits an analysed corpus of more than 20,000 Israeli households across 500+ municipalities, each a full hourly export from Israel Electric Corporation — up to 17,520 meter readings per home. That is what lets these tools answer with a number rather than a rule of thumb.

Ten read-only tools:

• compare_electricity_plans — rank every plan on the Israeli market by what it would save a specific household, per month and per year. Takes a monthly kWh figure or, far better, a 24-hour load curve.

• simulate_solar_tracks — price Israel's two mutually exclusive rooftop solar tracks against a real load shape, with payback and a recommendation. Which one pays more depends on WHEN a household consumes — the thing a roof-area calculator cannot see.

• get_city_consumption_benchmark — median monthly consumption, profile mix and 24-hour curve for a given Israeli city.

• get_national_load_curve — national demand by hour, day of week and season.

• classify_consumption_profile — classify a home as evening, night, morning, weekend or balanced, with peakiness and a night-shift opportunity figure.

• estimate_appliance_cost, size_air_conditioner, compare_ev_running_cost — running costs for appliances, air conditioning and electric cars at the current tariff.

• get_supplier_directory — every supplier and plan with its discount structure.

• how_to_export_my_iec_data — how a household downloads its own consumption file.

Privacy: no per-household data is reachable here. Every figure is either computed from the caller's own inputs or is a population aggregate published only where at least 25 analysed households sit behind it; a thinner cohort is refused rather than answered thinly. Nothing here writes, submits or contacts anyone.

Free, no account, no API key. Figures are in shekels and kWh.

Positive cards are celebrated, while challenging cards are explained directly without sugarcoating. Even unfamiliar tarot concepts are translated into clear, approachable language, creating a reading that feels personal, vivid, and relevant to your question.

Whether you are looking for free AI tarot, ChatGPT tarot, love tarot, reconciliation tarot, compatibility tarot, feelings tarot, career guidance, daily tarot, or one-card and three-card readings, Tarot by DoctorFortune lets you choose the cards yourself and enjoy a more engaging tarot experience. できること:
・Google・Bing・YouTube・Amazon・楽天などのサジェストキーワード取得
・独自データベースからの関連キーワード・よくある質問の取得
・LSIキーワード、他の人はこちらも質問（PAA）、同時ランクインキーワードといった関連トピックの探索
・月間検索数・SEO難易度・CPC・競合性の取得（月別推移つき）
・Google検索順位の実測
・競合分析: 任意のドメインが獲得しているキーワードと主力集客ページの抽出
・指定キーワードで検索流入を集めているページ・サイトの検索
・SEOライティング支援: 検索上位ページの見出し・共起語の抽出

活用例:
・SEO記事の構成案・タイトル・見出しの設計
・コンテンツ企画・ネタ出し、市場・需要調査
・競合サイトの自然検索の流入キーワード分析
・EC（Amazon・楽天）の商品リサーチ

日本の検索市場データに強みがあり、月間検索数の調査では海外の地域・言語の指定にも対応しています。利用にはラッコキーワードのアカウントが必要です。

plugins.name: app-6a86bb362da0819196ad522b5a73ce3b
plugins.displayName: 中央社新聞 CNA TAIWAN NEWS
plugins.description:
CNA provides a trusted, source-based news search and research service that allows users to search Central News Agency reporting directly within ChatGPT, stay informed about recent developments, and organize the evolving context surrounding specific people, events, and public issues.

Using natural language, users can search CNA news reports as well as content from CNA almanac, special features, and multilingual news coverage in English, Japanese, Indonesian, and other languages. The service also supports searches for standardized translations of foreign names and proper nouns, news photographs, government information, and fact-checking materials, helping users compare information across multiple sources and clarify uncertain claims. It can also organize retrieved information into event timelines, concise topic briefs, newspaper-style layouts, and relationship maps of people and organizations. These capabilities are suitable for news research, event retrospectives, issue tracking, information verification, content planning, and background research.

Responses preserve news headlines, publication dates, source information, and links to original articles whenever possible, allowing users to review the original reporting and conduct further verification. Some search results may come from government agencies, fact-checking organizations, contributed content, or other image sources; the system identifies their origins where available. The use and licensing of images remain subject to the terms, copyright requirements, and other applicable rules of their original sources.

plugins.displayName: 日本の補助金・公的支援検索
plugins.description:
Find Japanese grants and public support programs using official data published by government agencies.

Rather than simply listing programs, this app compares public company information with program requirements and clearly separates confirmed matches, possible mismatches, missing information, and official sources. This helps users understand why a program may be relevant and what still needs to be verified.

The app can be used by business owners and project leaders researching support for their own organizations, as well as by professional advisors researching programs for their clients or preparing for consultations.

When useful, it can also reference public corporate information and historical selection statistics, and organize unresolved questions into a consultation brief for a qualified professional.

Results are provided for research and decision support only. They do not guarantee eligibility, selection, funding amounts, or legal compliance. Before applying, always confirm the latest official guidelines and information published by the administering organization.

Primary official sources
- J-Grants
- gBizINFO
- National Tax Agency Corporate Number System
- Financial Services Agency EDINET
